title: Honest ATE Intervals under Symmetric Misclassification with a Weakening Validation Channel
banked_reason: The proved symmetric-experiment endpoint package is mathematically sound, but the sharp critical-window ratio and arbitrary vanishing-effect frontier remain open; paper_score_ceiling 6 < 7.4 leaves the run below the field floor with no bounded fix in scope.
gap_reasons: The recorded primary commitment is a sharp zero-effect critical-window expected-length/oracle-recovery characterization, but this node leaves that ratio and its needed quantile, count, and fourth-order corrections open; the delivered leading threshold is a weaker result.

The proposal commits to local-sequence expected-length characterization, whereas the core explicitly leaves arbitrary vanishing-effect sequences unresolved and proves only the zero-effect and fixed-away-from-zero endpoints.
Closest Tang--Qiu--Poon full theorem text remains inaccessible and the comparator_promise_table is empty.
proof_attempt_summary: Three proposal revisions and two D0 solve rounds established a mathematically sound symmetric-Bernoulli endpoint package: leading-exponent zero-effect bounds, oracle order, local-MSE behavior, and fixed-away-from-zero interval bounds. The field-level claim collapsed because the exact critical-window ratio and the full theta_n->0 transition were not derived, and narrowing to the endpoints would substitute the advertised kernel. A future re-raise should reuse the retained derivations and attack those two transition problems directly, while completing the closest-comparator source check.
tldr: In the bounded randomized symmetric-channel experiment, a globally honest ATE interval has proved matching three-scale expected-length bounds and a leading threshold at zero effect, together with a uniform known-channel benchmark. At effects bounded away from zero, its optimal length is of validation order even as reliability vanishes, so its oracle gap is comparable to \(G\). A finite-sample modulus resolves the separate local MSE question. Sharp transition-regime constants and the interval-length behavior for effects tending to zero remain open.
gap: The exact symmetric partial-validation likelihood and direct gold-standard measurements are prior art. The inspected Tang–Qiu–Poon article develops 12 interval procedures and empirically compares coverage, width, and location; its follow-up plans sample sizes for width and power. The separate question is the optimal pointwise expected length over intervals with unconditional full-rectangle coverage as reliability vanishes, and its known-channel oracle transition.
fill: Establish the finite-binary leading length bounds and leading weak-channel threshold with a total finite-sample interval; then determine the unresolved critical-window ratio and nonzero-effect length frontier. Keep local MSE on declared neighborhoods as a separate companion question.
